title: Shipping complex AI applications — Braintrust & Trainline
talk_summary: A Braintrust/Trainline workshop showing how to take a single-shot LLM call to a 5-stage tool-calling agent, then instrument it with tracing, build a golden eval set with deterministic + LLM-judge scorers, run offline experiments, and close the loop with online scoring on production traces. Trainline describes using offline evals to safely swap to cheaper models and to gate new features before shipping.

takeaways.technique: Offline eval gate before model downgrade
takeaways.what_they_do: Before switching to a cheaper model they run the candidate model against a stored golden dataset with the same scorers, compare scores to the current baseline, then confirm with online scoring after rollout.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've used Braintrust extensively to run offline evaluation and see what the effect is going to be and also online evaluation

takeaways.technique: Golden dataset from real failure modes, deterministic scorers first
takeaways.what_they_do: They seed a small dataset (10 cases) of edge cases, write cheap deterministic scorers (schema, category, escalation-reason present) and only use LLM-judge for nuance that can't be coded; failures found in production are replayed into the dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you cannot write it in a deterministic way, you want to be using LLM as a judge where possible

takeaways.what_they_do: Take a specific production failure, replay it as an eval case, tighten the prompt, re-run the eval across the whole set to check for regressions elsewhere, and diff experiment results before/after.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We want to tighten the prompt, run it again, and see uh what that looks like... across our entire test cases as well just to see if... we have regressed

takeaways.technique: Explicit staged decomposition over monolithic call
takeaways.what_they_do: They split one prompt into 5 named stages (collect context, triage, policy check, reply writer, escalate/finalize) so a failure localizes to a stage; they accept added latency as the tradeoff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this stage is slightly slow because we've broken down the individual one-shot LLM into sequential calls

takeaways.what_they_do: Run cheap deterministic scorers on 100% of production traces but sample expensive LLM-judge scoring at 5-10% once baseline confidence is established, starting high then reducing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you really want to reduce the the sampling rate down to 5 to 10%... deterministic scores, again, they're cheap. Recommend running them all all the time

takeaways.what_they_do: Prompts, tools and parameters are pushed to a central registry with slugs, version history and comments so non-engineers can change a model or prompt without code changes, and changes are diffable/reproducible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I didn't have to do any code changes. All I had to do was go into UI, change the model I wanted to
